headline: Japan will provide up to $21 billion to build two new GlobalFoundries chip factories in Malta, New York, and the US government will receive shares in the company.
score_reason: Lowered from 7 to 6: the announcement was made on 14 Oct, three days before this edition, and no earlier edition carried it.
importance_line: It adds a Japanese-funded source of chips for cars, industrial equipment and telecoms in the US and puts the government on the company's share register, but the plants are years away and the size of the stake rests on Bloomberg's report.
summary: The Associated Press reports that GlobalFoundries, a US chipmaker, said on 14 Oct 2026 it will open two factories in Malta, New York, financed by up to $21 billion from Japan under the US-Japan trade agreement, with about $10 billion going to a first plant due to open in 2029 and about $10 billion to a second. President Donald Trump said the US government will receive shares in the company, which Bloomberg, as relayed by Seoul Economic Daily, puts at a 4 percent stake.
notes: Pool source WSJ (HTTP 401) and Reuters unreadable here; AP text read on news-herald.com, Bloomberg details from Seoul Economic Daily (en.sedaily.com/international/2026/10/15/japan-to-invest-21-billion-in-two-globalfoundries-chip). Pool date 17 Oct is wrong; the news broke on 14 Oct 2026. Event older than the window; the editor decides whether it prints.
